theorem_title: Theorem 1.1 — sparse expanding codes with polynomial stretch and arbitrary near-half errors
formal_statement:
namespace ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch

/-- Theorem 1.1: constant arity, polynomial stretch and runtime, and the unconditional
near-half arbitrary-error test. The absolute arity constant precedes ε. -/
theorem expanding_codes :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ (k : ℕ) (m : ℕ → ℕ) (P : ∀ n, PMF (Generator (m n) n))
        (D : ∀ n, Word (m n) → Bool),
        (k : ℝ) ≤ C * ε⁻¹ ^ 6 ∧ EfficientFamily ε k m P D := by sorry

end ExpandingCodes.PolynomialStretch
natural_language_statement:
There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every real $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ there are an integer $k\le C\varepsilon^{-6}$, a deterministic row-count function $m(n)$, a randomized matrix sampler and a deterministic test $D$. For every sufficiently large $n$,
$$n<m(n)<n^k,\qquad m(n)=n^{O_\varepsilon(1)}.$$
The sampler runs in $\operatorname{poly}_\varepsilon(n)$ time on every unbiased random tape, with exactly the stated output law on binary matrices $G\in\mathbb F_2^{m(n)\times n}$. Every output has row weight exactly $k$, and
$$\Pr[G\text{ is }(1-\varepsilon,k,n^{1-\varepsilon})\text{-expanding}]\ge1-n^{-1/\varepsilon}.$$
The test runs in deterministic $\operatorname{poly}_\varepsilon(m,n)$ time. For every sampler output, every binary message $x$ and every binary error $e$ with $|\operatorname{supp}(e)|\le(1/2-\varepsilon)m$,
$$D(Gx+e)=1,\qquad\Pr[D(U_m)=1]\le\exp(-\varepsilon^2m/128).$$
The error may depend arbitrarily on the message and on the sampled matrix. Constants, programs and the eventual size threshold are fixed before $n$, the matrix and its random bits; $k$ does not depend on $n$.

This is the headline existence theorem. The construction milestone supplies its witnesses without restricting $\varepsilon$ to rational values or assuming successful expansion.

Differences from the source:
- encoding: randomized polynomial-time sampler and deterministic polynomial-time test → fixed finite transition tables, a polynomial-length unbiased tape, exact output law, and worst-case transition bounds; reason: this spells out the algorithmic existence clauses with no advice, runtime annotation or correctness assumption
- encoding: m=n^{O_ε(1)}>n depending only on n,ε and m<n^k → a deterministic function m with n<m(n)<n^k eventually; reason: k is fixed before n, so the same displayed bound already gives polynomial growth
- encoding: exp(−Ω_ε(m)) → exp(−ε²m/128) eventually; reason: the construction uses a fixed rational θ between ε/2 and ε; the source proof rate θ²/32 gives the displayed ε-rate
